comments.content: When initializing from another context, this drops that context's default schema and explicitly passes `null` to `setDefaultCatalog`; it also does nothing when only a schema is available. Consequently, auxiliary/new execution contexts can run unqualified SQL against the driver's default schema rather than the schema selected in the source context. Preserve `executionMetaContext.getDefaultSchema()` when setting the catalog (and handle the schema-only case), or delegate the state copying to the superclass.

Do not swallow this `DBCException`. Callers of `setDefaultCatalog` will treat a failed catalog switch as successful, while `activeCatalogName` remains unchanged, leaving the UI/context state inconsistent without reporting the failure. Remove the catch or rethrow after logging.
